rq: joint identification of raw-language equivalence and latent intervention-target partition

primary_prior_art.title: Finite state space non parametric Hidden Markov Models are in general identifiable

finding: Finite-state nonparametric HMM transition and emission laws are identifiable up to hidden-state permutation under full-rank/separation assumptions; sequential dependence alone is therefore not an open identifiability obstacle. However, the identifiable predictive state can over-refine semantics and does not by itself identify an internal raw-language quotient, intervention-target quotient, or denotation map.
counterexample: An identifiable HMM may split one semantic target into context-specific predictive states, or admit different internal Q/P/d factorizations that integrate to the same state-specific joint emission and transition law. Exact transition/emission aliasing also preserves merge/split ontologies.
next_positive_obligation: Identify or refute an identifiable semantic quotient of recovered sequential predictive states, or preregister a theorem-boundary public HMM baseline with direct utterance-partition, target-partition, and quotient-map metrics.
